annotations.title: Fortress Shield: redact PII/secrets (free, on this Worker)

description:
WHAT: Fortress Shield (agent I/O PII protection). Return sanitized copies of texts with every local PII/secret finding replaced: placeholder [EMAIL_k7q2m9xp4a] (random id per value), mask, or hash. For placeholders the originals come back only inside meta.sealed_map, an AES-256-GCM encrypted string that this Worker opens in pii_restore_text. The originals stay out of the model context.
WHEN: Right before sending user data to an LLM/third party. Keep meta.sealed_map if you need to restore originals in the LLM answer later.
WHEN NOT: For a findings report only use pii_scan_text. For names/addresses NER, URLs or PDFs use pii_guard_documents (paid).
COST: Free; no token.
RETURNS: One "redacted_document" row per text with output_text, typed_placeholders_escaped, context_lowered and context_suppressed; meta.sealed_map (placeholder style, "fqs2.…"; null plus a SEAL_KEY_NOT_CONFIGURED note when this deployment has no seal key) and meta.seal {algorithm, entries, expires_at, restore_bound, max_restores}. Errors: INPUT_TOO_LARGE, INVALID_PATTERN, INVALID_ARGUMENT, SEALED_MAP_INVALID, SEALED_MAP_EXPIRED, SEAL_KEY_NOT_CONFIGURED, RESTORE_KEY_REQUIRED / RESTORE_KEY_MISMATCH (priorSealedMap bound to another restore key).
BEHAVIOR: Placeholder ids are random on every call unless you pass priorSealedMap; "hash" is random per call unless a hash key is set. The sealed_map is bound to the restore key header of this request (X-FQ-PII-Restore-Key, set by the operator in the client connection); without one, pii_restore_text reports counts only. Runs on this Fairquery-hosted Worker (Cloudflare), not on the caller's machine; inputs leave the client. This Worker's code is designed not to store inputs, results, or an Apify token. No further network call; texts are not forwarded. Milliseconds.
PARAMETERS: texts: one element per document, 500,000 chars in total; the same value gets the same placeholder in every document of one call, and case/format variants share it (JANE@ACME.COM and jane@acme.com; +1 415 555 0100 and (415) 555-0100). Placeholder-shaped text already in the input (a user typing "[EMAIL_1]") is itself replaced by a [TYPED_PLACEHOLDER_<id>] placeholder and restored verbatim, so it can never pull another value. priorSealedMap: the meta.sealed_map of an earlier call; values seen before keep their placeholder, new ones are added, and the returned sealed_map covers both (use it across turns and when paging). redactionStyle: "placeholder" is the only reversible style; "mask" keeps a few characters for human review; "hash" with hashKey (16-256 chars, your own key) gives the same output for the same value in every call (HMAC-SHA256, joinable), without hashKey the salt is random per call. sealTtlHours: how long the sealed_map opens (1-720, default 24). returnPlaceholderMap: deprecated and refused unless the request carries the restore key header; use sealed_map. maxRestores: restore cap for this sealed_map (default 3). entityTypes / allowList / allowDomains / allowPatterns / customDetectors / contextScoring / contextMode / entropyScan / defaultPhoneRegion: identical semantics to pii_scan_text. limit/offset page whole documents (one item per text, default 50 = all).
EXAMPLE: {"texts":["Call +1 415 555 0100 or mail jane@acme.com"]} -> output_text "Call [PHONE_4hq8m2xk9c] or mail [EMAIL_t7c3pz2wqa]", meta.sealed_map "fqs2.…".

allowDomains.description: Optional, default []. 0-200 email domains whose addresses are never flagged; subdomains included. Example: ["yourco.com"] exempts support@yourco.com and a@eu.yourco.com

allowList.description: Optional, default [] (nothing exempt). 0-500 exact values (<= 500 chars each) that are never flagged; whole-value, case-insensitive match, not substring. Example: ["support@yourco.com","192.0.2.1"]

allowPatterns.description: Optional, default []. 0-50 JavaScript regular expressions (<= 200 chars; no backreferences or nested quantifiers -> INVALID_PATTERN); a finding whose value matches any of them is not flagged. Example: ["^192\.0\.2\.","@example\.(com|org)$"]

contextMode.description: Optional, "lower" | "drop", default "lower". What happens to a match that only a negative context word argues against: "lower" still flags/redacts it with confidence "low" and context "negative:<reason>" (counted in context_lowered); "drop" (strict precision) leaves it untouched (counted in context_suppressed).

contextScoring.description: Optional boolean, default true. true uses the words around a match: labels like "SSN:", "phone:", "my cell", "call me" raise confidence, and a label earlier on the same line wins over a negative word. "version"/"v" before an IPv4 or phone-shaped number and "invoice"/"order"/"ticket"/"ref" before a bare phone-shaped number lower it (see contextMode). Phones with +country code, parentheses or two separators, and IPv4 with a port, CIDR suffix or 3-digit octet are never lowered. false = format-only scoring.

customDetectors.description: Optional, default []. 0-20 of your own detectors (regex pattern and/or terms dictionary) for account IDs, ticket formats or member numbers; findings use your type name with category "custom" and are redacted and restored like built-in types.

pattern.description: Optional JavaScript regular expression (<= 200 chars; no backreferences or nested quantifiers). Example: "\bMBR-\d{8}\b"

terms.description: Optional dictionary: 0-500 literal terms matched as whole words. Example: ["Project Bluebird"]

type.description: Type name for this detector, 2-40 chars, letters/digits/_ (uppercased in output). Example: "MEMBER_ID"

defaultPhoneRegion.description: Optional, default "US". ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (2 letters, pattern ^[A-Za-z]{2}$, case-insensitive) used only for phone numbers written without a +country prefix. Examples: "US", "DE", "GB"

entityTypes.description: Optional, default omitted = every free-tool detector (pii_list_detectors rows with local:true). 0-40 detector type names (<= 40 chars, case-insensitive), e.g. ["EMAIL","CREDIT_CARD","AWS_ACCESS_KEY"]. Valid values: the "type" field of those rows; unknown names match nothing (no error)

entropyScan.description: Optional boolean, default false. true also flags unlabeled random-looking tokens of 20-200 chars as HIGH_ENTROPY_STRING (catches unknown key formats; may flag hashes/UUIDs). Example: true

hashKey.description: Optional, hash style only, discouraged. Your own 16-256 char key for deterministic HMAC-SHA256 hashes. As an argument it sits in the model context (HASHKEY_ARG_IN_CONTEXT note); prefer the X-FQ-PII-Hash-Key request header set in the MCP client connection, which wins when both are present. Never returned.

limit.description: Optional page size: items to return, integer 1-50 (default 50). Example: 50

maxRestores.description: Optional integer 1-100, default 3. How many pii_restore_text calls may return original values for this sealed_map; later calls report counts only (RESTORE_LIMIT_REACHED).

offset.description: Optional zero-based number of items to skip, integer 0-1000000 (default 0); pass nextOffset from the previous response, e.g. 100

priorSealedMap.description: Optional. meta.sealed_map from an earlier pii_redact_text call (placeholder style only). Keeps the same placeholder for values seen before. Example: "fqs1.…"

redactionStyle.description: Optional, one of "placeholder" | "mask" | "hash", default "placeholder". "placeholder" = [EMAIL_k7q2m9xp4a] (reversible with meta.sealed_map); "mask" = j***@a***.com, **** **** **** 1111; "hash" = [EMAIL:3f2a9c0d1b7e] (salted sha256 prefix; with hashKey an HMAC that stays the same across calls). Example: "mask"

returnPlaceholderMap.description: Optional boolean, default false. Deprecated: true (placeholder style only) asks for meta.placeholder_map {"[EMAIL_…]":"jane@acme.com"} with the ORIGINAL values in clear text; honoured only when the request carries the operator restore key header or sealing is unavailable (otherwise a PLAINTEXT_MAP_REFUSED note). Prefer meta.sealed_map.

sealTtlHours.description: Optional integer 1-720, default 24. Hours until meta.sealed_map stops opening.

texts.description: Required. 1-50 documents (prompt, chat message, log, file content), each <= 200,000 chars, total <= 500,000 chars. Example: ["Mail jane@acme.com, key AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"]

name: pii_redact_text

count.description: Number of items in this page

hasMore.description: True if more items exist after this page

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null

offset.description: Offset of the first item in this page
